$comment: Editorial DTP comparison matrix behind /docs/paged/compare. Ordinal 0-3 editorial scores on a dated snapshot, NOT vendor benchmarks. Roadmap-not-shipped Paged capabilities use pagedPlanned:true and are scored honestly, not as present. Update with `pnpm update:comparison` (researches current facts via Claude Opus) or by hand — then bump `snapshot`.

rows.note: Paged is MPL-2.0 OR PMEL; Scribus is GPL. Affinity is free-of-charge but proprietary and vendor-governed (Canva).
Paged's .paged is always a valid IDML (ZIP) package. InDesign's .indd is closed (IDML is its interchange form). .qxp and .af are proprietary; Scribus .sla is open XML but app-specific.

rows.dimension: Round-trips IDML with the InDesign ecosystem
rows.note: InDesign defines IDML. Paged reads and writes it natively. Affinity imports IDML but cannot export it; Scribus IDML import is partial.
Paged exposes a sandboxed paged.* ECMAScript surface (emerging). InDesign has ExtendScript/UXP; Scribus has Python; Affinity has no scripting.
Paged ships a public plugin SDK (emerging). InDesign's SDK is mature but closed/paid; Quark has XTensions; Affinity has no plugins.
InDesign leans on InDesign Server + EasyCatalog/priint. Paged is automation-native and headless-friendly by design; parts of the batch pipeline are still landing.
Paged renders with WebGPU and runs in the browser as well as headless. The incumbents are desktop apps (InDesign adds a server product).
The honest gap: Paged is an emerging platform, not at the layout/typography depth of 25-year-old incumbents. Treated as baseline because every serious tool clears it.
Scribus is notably strong here. Paged color/print production is emerging; several pieces are on the roadmap, not shipped.

verdicts.choose: Choose InDesign for the deepest layout toolset, ecosystem, and talent pool — if a subscription and a closed format are acceptable.
Choose QuarkXPress for long-document and structured/enterprise publishing on a perpetual licence.
Choose Affinity for a free, polished one-off layout app — but accept a proprietary format, no scripting, and no plugins.
Choose Scribus for mature, open-source layout with excellent print/color output today.
Choose Paged for an open, IDML-compatible, scriptable, automation-first foundation — accepting that layout/print depth is still emerging.
